filings.business_summary: NIKE, Inc. designs, develops, markets and sells athletic footwear, apparel, equipment and accessories under the NIKE, Jordan and Converse brands. Sales go through wholesale accounts and NIKE Direct (owned stores plus digital). It describes itself as the world's largest seller of athletic footwear and apparel (SEC 10-K 2026-07-15, Item 1). FY2026 (year ended May 31, 2026) revenue was $46.4B, flat reported and down 2% currency-neutral. Net income was $3.1B and diluted EPS $2.10 (SEC 10-K). The company is in a multi-year reset: it is rebalancing footwear supply, repositioning NIKE Digital as full-price, reinvesting in wholesale and cutting costs. Greater China and Converse are weak (Greater China -26% and Converse -28% currency-neutral in Q1 FY27, SEC 10-Q 2026-10-02). In October 2026 NIKE announced the 'Pace' program: about $1.0B of further pre-tax charges and about $2.5B of cumulative savings through FY2031 (SEC 10-Q). Stock price is $34.61 and market cap about $51.4B (Market Data).

filings.growth_rationale: This is a judgment call, not a company forecast. NIKE gives no FCF guidance in the material. FCF has fallen from $6.6B (FY24) to $2.2B (FY26) as revenue fell 10% in FY25 and operating income dropped from $6.3B to $3.7B. Q1 FY27 shows no recovery yet: revenue -4%, OCF $135M, implied FCF about -$64M. Arguments for growth from a depressed base: (a) management targets about $2.5B cumulative pre-tax savings through FY31, roughly $0.5B a year on average, before charges and reinvestment; (b) FY26 OCF was held down by working capital, with receivables up $1.2B including the IEEPA receivable that was largely collected after year-end, though Q1 FY27 shows other offsets from compensation and tax payments; (c) North America and wholesale are growing and gross margin is up 60 bps in Q1. Arguments against: Greater China and Converse are expected to stay negative through FY27, Sportswear and Jordan actions extend beyond FY27, about $1.0B of cash restructuring charges are coming, capex rose to $684M, and dividends already exceed FCF. FY26 operating income and gross profit also include a $986M one-time tariff recovery. I use a moderate 6% for the first five years. It sits between a recovery case (well above 10% off a trough base) and a stagnation case, and I give it low confidence.

Market Data: 4-year FCF, operating income and revenue history
Analyst growth estimates: not available (Yahoo Finance Analysis page shows no data)
stated_risks: Intense competition in athletic footwear, apparel and equipment, including adidas, Anta, ASICS, Deckers, Li Ning, lululemon, New Balance, On, Puma, Under Armour and VF (SEC 10-K, Item 1/1A)

Execution risk in the product, marketplace and brand reset: lower footwear supply, markdowns, higher returns and discounts. Management says actions will 'adversely affect' revenue and profitability, extend beyond FY27 for Sportswear and Jordan, and that Greater China and Converse will keep dragging through FY27 (SEC 10-K; SEC 10-Q)
Greater China weakness: declining traffic, elevated promotions and high marketplace inventory. Q1 FY27 revenue was -26% currency-neutral (SEC 10-Q)
Tariff and trade-policy risk. Sourcing is concentrated: Vietnam makes 52% of footwear, Indonesia 27% and China 16%, and four footwear contract manufacturers make about 60% of production (SEC 10-K)
Pace program risk: savings may not materialize, charges are preliminary and may rise, and the new three-geography structure could disrupt operations (SEC 10-Q)
Management transition: CFO Matthew Friend left in August/September 2026 and David Denton now signs as CFO. A new COO was appointed December 2025 (SEC 10-K; SEC 10-Q)

Tax risk: $953M gross unrecognized tax benefits, an IRS audit of FY2017-2023, the European Commission State Aid investigation, and Pillar Two changes. Income taxes were the auditor's critical audit matter (SEC 10-K)
Belgian customs claim for alleged underpaid duties since FY2018, with no loss estimate given and a possible material effect (SEC 10-K Note 16; SEC 10-Q Note 11)
Multiple securities class action and shareholder derivative suits relating to the stock price drop (SEC 10-K, Item 1A)
Credit ratings were downgraded in 2025, though still A+/A2 (SEC 10-K)
Control and overhang: Swoosh, LLC owns about 79% of Class A; Class A holders elect three-quarters of the board; a large sale could depress the stock (SEC 10-K)
Heavy fixed commitments: $15.5B endorsement obligations, $4.9B product purchase obligations, $2.4B other purchase obligations and about $3.1B lease liabilities (SEC 10-K)
Inventory forecasting and obsolescence risk; inventory $7.8B at Aug 31, 2026, up 5% vs May 31 (SEC 10-K; SEC 10-Q)
AI-driven shifts in consumer shopping and AI-related cyber, privacy and IP risks (SEC 10-K, Item 1A)

accounting_red_flags.flag: One-time $986M IEEPA tariff recovery inflates FY26 cost of sales, gross profit and operating income
accounting_red_flags.evidence: Q4 FY26 benefit of $986M in cost of sales, of which $965M North America, recorded when recovery was 'deemed probable'. North America gross margin rose 210 bps to 45.6%. Management says it 'largely offset' IEEPA tariff costs incurred in FY26, but the gross cost incurred is not quantified in the material. $684M was still a receivable at year-end. Operating income of $3,797M and reported 42.9% gross margin include this item; the gross margin would be about 40.8% without it (calculated), if offsetting tariff costs are ignored.

accounting_red_flags.flag: Receivables grew far faster than revenue; cash conversion weak
accounting_red_flags.evidence: Accounts receivable $5,931M vs $4,717M (+25.7%) while revenue grew 0.2%. Excluding the $684M IEEPA receivable, receivables were about $5,247M (+11%, calculated), against wholesale revenue +6%. OCF fell to $2,868M from $3,698M; FCF $2,184M is below net income $3,108M.
accounting_red_flags.source: SEC 10-K (2026-07-15), balance sheet, cash flow statement, MD&A

accounting_red_flags.flag: Sales-related reserves and inventory reserve declined while management says returns and discounts are rising
accounting_red_flags.evidence: Sales-related reserves fell from $1,834M to $1,589M and the returns reserve from $1,277M to $1,099M, while wholesale revenue rose 6% and management cites 'higher sales returns and discounts with our wholesale partners'. Inventory reserve fell from $233M to $213M with inventory flat at $7.5B. Converse's gross margin cites 'higher inventory obsolescence reserves'. Reserve releases support margin and revenue, and judgment is involved (critical accounting estimates).

FY24 restructuring $443M, FY26 severance $385M, and a new Pace program with about $1.0B further pre-tax charges through FY31. FY26 charges were split between operating overhead and cost of sales ($154M in cost of sales). The 10-K says 'may take additional actions'. EBIT is not adjusted for these charges, but cash costs will weigh on FCF.

accounting_red_flags.flag: Effective tax rate volatility and a rising valuation allowance
accounting_red_flags.evidence: ETR was 20.3% in FY26 vs 17.1% in FY25 (which included a $133M one-time deferred tax benefit) and 14.9% in FY24. The valuation allowance rose from $51M to $192M. Unrecognized tax benefits were $953M plus $438M accrued interest and penalties. Tax holiday benefit was $254M. Income taxes were the auditor's critical audit matter. Q1 FY27 ETR was 22.7% on foreign audit settlements.
accounting_red_flags.source: SEC 10-K (2026-07-15), Note 7 and auditor report; SEC 10-Q (2026-10-02), Note 4

accounting_red_flags.flag: Dividend exceeds free cash flow; capital allocation destroyed value
accounting_red_flags.evidence: FY26 dividends paid were $2,407M against FCF of $2,184M, and Q1 FY27 FCF was about -$64M against $610M of dividends (calculated). The company bought back 124.4M shares at an average of $97.57 (about $12.1B), against the current price of $34.61, and stock options average $96.44 strike (76.8M outstanding), so they are far out of the money.
accounting_red_flags.source: SEC 10-K (2026-07-15) cash flow statement and Note 9; SEC 10-Q (2026-10-02); Market Data

accounting_red_flags.flag: Supplier finance programs flatter working capital
accounting_red_flags.evidence: About $1.1B of confirmed supplier obligations sit in accounts payable of $3.6B (about 30%, calculated). About $11.5B of invoices were confirmed in FY26. Payment terms are not disclosed, so the effect on OCF cannot be sized.

accounting_red_flags.flag: Stock-based compensation is large relative to FCF
accounting_red_flags.evidence: SBC of $715M is added back in OCF and equals about 33% of FY26 FCF (calculated). The cash flow statement shows net share issuance proceeds of $354M versus almost no repurchases.
accounting_red_flags.source: SEC 10-K (2026-07-15), cash flow statement and Note 9

accounting_red_flags.flag: Finance leadership change immediately after the 10-K
accounting_red_flags.evidence: CFO Matthew Friend signed the 10-K on July 15, 2026 and ceased being CFO on August 17, 2026, with separation on September 4, 2026. David Denton signed the Q1 10-Q as CFO (offer letter dated June 16, 2026). A new COO was appointed in December 2025 and a Chief Legal Officer in 2024. The Chief Accounting Officer is a signatory.
accounting_red_flags.source: SEC 10-K (2026-07-15), executive officers footnote and exhibit list; SEC 10-Q (2026-10-02), signatures

accounting_red_flags.flag: Unquantified contingent liability: Belgian customs claim
accounting_red_flags.evidence: The company cannot estimate a range of loss; bank guarantees of $1.3B (vs $0.9B prior year) were outstanding, though these cover several items. An adverse outcome 'could have a material adverse effect'. No accrual is disclosed.

accounting_red_flags.flag: Non-GAAP ROIC definition may flatter returns
accounting_red_flags.evidence: ROIC of 18.7% subtracts all cash and short-term investments from invested capital and includes operating leases in debt. The tax adjustment applies the effective tax rate to EBIT. On the company's own definition ROIC fell from 20.2%, while EBIT margin is 8.3% vs 12.7% in FY24.

accounting_red_flags.flag: Hedge gains in cost of sales collapsed, shifting reported margin
accounting_red_flags.evidence: Cash flow hedge gains reclassified to cost of sales fell from $295M in FY25 to $20M in FY26, and to a $30M loss in Q1 FY27. FX effects are listed as a gross margin driver of +20 bps in FY26 and +40 bps in Q1 FY27, and corporate segment results swing with standard-rate differences.
accounting_red_flags.source: SEC 10-K (2026-07-15), Note 12 and MD&A; SEC 10-Q (2026-10-02), Note 7 and MD&A

data_gaps: No analyst consensus, growth estimates or management FCF guidance in the material. The Yahoo Finance Analysis page shows only a blank estimates table, and the source of the 20.3x forward P/E is not provided.
Gross cost of IEEPA tariffs incurred in FY26 is not quantified, so the net effect of the $986M recovery on underlying margins cannot be calculated.
Q1 FY27 normalized FCF cannot be derived; the split between permanent and timing items in working capital is not given.
Market Data total debt of $11,125M differs slightly from balance sheet debt plus lease liabilities ($11,072M at Aug 31, 2026). The exact composition used by Market Data is not documented.
Market Data capex/OCF/FCF figures are labeled by fiscal year-end dates (2023-05-31 to 2026-05-31). FY2023 figures cannot be reconciled to the provided filings, which cover FY2024-FY2026.
Supplier finance payment terms and actual effect on operating cash flow are not disclosed.
Q2 FY27 and later guidance, plus the timing of Pace savings versus reinvestment, is not given. The $2.5B savings figure is cumulative, pre-charge and pre-reinvestment.
Belgian customs claim: no loss range, accrual or timeline is disclosed.
Tariff-related cost trends beyond the IEEPA ruling (for example other tariff regimes) are not quantified.
Proxy statement (executive compensation, related-party transactions) is incorporated by reference and not provided.
No peer valuation or industry data is provided for relative valuation.

sources_of_moat: Brand intangible asset: the largest athletic brand, with Nike, Jordan and Converse. Brand value is cited above $50B versus about $16B for Adidas.
Scale: FY26 revenue of $46.4B is almost twice Adidas's revenue. That gives Nike purchasing, sourcing and marketing leverage, plus athlete and team endorsement reach.
Performance product and innovation pipeline: Performance revenue is about $16B and grew high single digits in Q1 FY27 across running, football, basketball, tennis and golf.
Distribution breadth: sales in nearly 190 countries, owned stores plus wholesale, and the Nike app and SNKRS data. Nike is rebuilding wholesale partnerships.
moat.evidence: The moat is real but weaker than it was. Consumer switching costs are negligible (cited by koalagains.com), so it rests almost entirely on brand and scale. Revenue fell from $51.4B in FY24 to $46.4B in FY26. EBIT margin fell from 12.7% to 8.3% and FCF margin from about 12.9% to about 4.7% (from the supplied filings summary). Euromonitor puts Nike's 2025 global sports-footwear share at 22.9%, down from 25.9%. Adidas rose from 11.7% to 12.2% (founderpin.com, citing Euromonitor). On, Hoka, New Balance and Asics are growing faster, though from much smaller bases. Management guides FY27 revenue down high single digits. Q1 FY27 Sportswear fell low double digits, Jordan fell mid-teens and Greater China fell 26%. Nike still has gross margin of about 43% and net cash, so the franchise is not broken. A wide moat is not supported by current results. Narrow is a judgment call.

management.capital_allocation: Mixed. The ~$12.1B of buybacks to date were done at an average of about $97.57 a share, against a current price of about $34.61. Repurchases have been paused since Q1 FY26. FY26 dividends of $2,407M exceeded FCF of $2,184M, so the payout is not covered by FCF right now. Capex rose to $684M. The new Pace program costs about $1.0B in charges for about $2.5B of savings through FY31 (CNBC and the earnings-call summaries). Net cash is a plus: $8.4B of cash and short-term investments, with leverage of about 2x (Yahoo/GuruFocus call summary). Management has cut SG&A, with Q1 SG&A down 3%. It also admitted it underappreciated the need to split Sportswear into smaller consumer segments (TradingKey transcript summary). CEO Elliott Hill's 'Sport Offense' and the wholesale reset are showing results in Performance categories. The turnaround is taking longer than expected, and Denton (CFO) warned that the actions will weigh on results into FY28. A new CFO, David Denton, has just joined. Execution on the reset has not yet been shown.
governance_concerns: Dual-class structure: Class A holders elect 8 of 11 directors and public Class B holders elect only 3 (Forbes, Stocktitan DEF 14A).

Control: Swoosh LLC (Phil Knight) owns 78.8% of Class A. Phil Knight owns another 9.8% and a Travis Knight trust owns 8.8% (Forbes). The Knight family holds about 97% of Class A, roughly 21% of total economic value (whoistheownerof.com).

A shareholder proposal for a dual-class sunset provision was filed by the New York City pension funds. Swoosh said it would vote against it and had no plans to implement it (Forbes). This leaves activism with little leverage.
Board independence: Travis Knight is not independent under NYSE rules, and Phil Knight is Chairman Emeritus with a standing observer invitation (DEF 14A).
Capital allocation and the long price decline, with about $12B of buybacks done at roughly three times today's price, remain open questions for public shareholders.

industry.growth_outlook: Mixed. A third-party source cites global sportswear market growth of 7.2% in 2025 (sinofinetex.com, lower-quality). Nike's own FY27 revenue is guided to fall high single digits, with adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.35. Q1 FY27 Performance grew high single digits, but Sportswear, Jordan and China fell. Long-term industry growth beyond this is unknown.
industry.competitive_intensity: High and rising. Share is moving to running specialists and resurgent rivals. A third-party source (businessmodelanalyst.com) reports On grew about 30%, New Balance about 20%, Asics about 20%, Hoka 16% and Adidas 13%. Nike shrank 10% in its most recent full year. Adidas has regained lifestyle share through Samba and Gazelle. Local players such as Anta compete in China. Discounting is rising, and Q1 gross margin rose 60 bps despite higher discounts.

catalysts: Growth in Performance categories (running, football, basketball, tennis, golf), which was up high single digits in Q1 FY27 and was $16B in FY26
Pace productivity program: about $2.5B of cumulative savings through FY31 against about $1.0B of charges
Stabilising Sportswear and Jordan, including the cut in Dunk supply of nearly 50%, and a cleaner wholesale channel
China marketplace reset. Management expects China to get worse for the balance of FY27 before it stabilises, so this is a later catalyst.
Reorganisation into three geographies (Americas, APGC, EMEA) from FY28, and a new campus in Bengaluru
Gross margin recovery: Q1 FY27 gross margin was 42.8%, up 60 bps
Possible resumption of buybacks (about $5.9B authorisation remains) once FCF recovers
Activism is a possible but difficult catalyst given the dual-class structure

bear_case: The base-case DCF starts from $4.023B of FCF. That figure is the FY24–FY26 three-year average, since (6.617+3.268+2.184)/3 = 4.023. It includes the FY24 peak of $6.6B and is about 84% above the latest FCF of $2.184B. FCF has fallen three years in a row (6.6 → 3.3 → 2.2), and Q1 FY27 was about -$64M. Rescaling the model's own outputs to $2.184B gives roughly $23 for base, about $13 for bear and about $33 for bull (my own arithmetic, not from the filings). That puts base about 33% below the $34.05 price, and even the bull case only about matches it. The +27% upside comes from the starting point, not the business.

Management guides FY27 revenue down high single digits and adjusted EPS to $1.15–1.35, versus $2.10 in FY26. That is a decline of roughly 36–45%. Q1 EPS was already $0.48, so the guide leaves only about $0.67–0.87 for the last three quarters, or roughly $0.22–0.29 a quarter. That is far below Q1's $0.48 run-rate. On guided EPS the stock trades at about 25–30x, not the 16x trailing or 20x 'forward' shown. A model that grows FCF 6% a year from an average base ignores the guidance of a steep near-term earnings drop.

The dividend is not covered. FY26 dividends were $2,407M against FCF of $2,184M and net income of $3,108M. Q1 FY27 dividends were $610M against FCF of about -$64M. At the guided EPS of $1.15–1.35, the roughly $1.62 per share dividend is a payout above 100% of earnings. About $2.0B of debt is current, about $1.0B of Pace cash charges are coming, and capex is rising. The likely outcomes are a dividend cut, more debt, or a drawdown of cash, and none of these supports value. The 4.8% yield is a risk, not a cushion.

FY26 earnings quality is flattered. Operating income of $3,797M is up only 2.6% year on year, but it includes the $986M one-time IEEPA tariff credit. Without it, operating income is about $2.8B, down about 24%. Gross margin would be about 40.8% versus 42.7% a year earlier, a decline of about 190 bps, not the +20 bps reported. EV/EBITDA of 11x and the 16x trailing P/E both rest on this inflated base. Adjusting EBITDA for the credit puts the multiple nearer 14x.

The Q1 gross margin gain of 60 bps looks low quality. Of that, 40 bps is attributed to FX, and hedge gains in cost of sales swung from +$295M (FY25) to +$20M (FY26) to a $30M loss in Q1 FY27. Sales-related reserves fell 13% and the inventory reserve fell from $233M to $213M, even though management cites higher returns and discounts. Inventory rose 5% in Q1 while revenue fell 4%. A markdown cycle and more reserve builds look likely, which would hit margins.

The moat is eroding in the data. Euromonitor puts Nike's sports-footwear share at 22.9%, down from 25.9%. Sportswear fell low double digits in Q1 and Jordan fell mid-teens. Greater China was -26%, with EBIT -34%, and Converse was -28%. Competitors are growing 13–30% (low-quality sources) in a market said to be growing about 7%. Switching costs are negligible. Only Performance, at about $16B, is growing, and it is a minority of revenue.

Management and governance give public holders little protection. Buybacks of about $12.1B were done at an average of $97.57, nearly 3x today's price. The CFO signed the 10-K on July 15 and left on August 17, and a new CFO signed the 10-Q. A new $1.0B restructuring was announced two months later. This is the second large charge program in three years (FY24 $443M, FY26 $385M). The Knight family and Swoosh control Class A and elect 8 of 11 directors, and Swoosh has said it will vote against a sunset provision. An activist cannot force change. The tax profile is also uncertain: $953M of unrecognized tax benefits, an IRS audit, EU State Aid and a Belgian customs claim with no loss estimate.

The Pace savings of $2.5B are cumulative through FY31, which is only about $0.5B a year. They are pre-reinvestment and come with about $1.0B of charges. The savings are small against the roughly $2.4–2.9B drop in operating income since FY24. Management also warns that actions will weigh on results into FY28. A 5-year 6% FCF growth path therefore looks too early.

assumption_challenges.assumption: Base FCF of $4.023B (the three-year average) as the DCF starting point.
assumption_challenges.why_questionable: It is not trailing FCF, and it is not normalized FCF either. It is 84% above FY26 FCF of $2.184B and includes the FY24 peak of $6.6B, which came before revenue fell 10% and margins compressed. The filings summary itself cites FY26 FCF of $2.18B, a 4.2% yield, and Q1 FY27 FCF of about -$64M. The valuation inputs contradict the stated facts. Using FY26 FCF cuts every scenario by about 46% before the net-debt adjustment.

assumption_challenges.assumption: 6% FCF growth for five years, described as 'moderate' and 'between recovery and stagnation'.
assumption_challenges.why_questionable: It is applied on top of an already-recovered base, so the effective recovery is much larger. Guidance is for FY27 revenue down high single digits and EPS down about 40%. China and Converse are expected to worsen through FY27, Sportswear and Jordan actions run past FY27, and Q1 revenue was -4% and OCF was $135M. The rationale itself admits low confidence and no analyst or management FCF guidance. The bear case of 2% growth also uses the inflated $4.0B base, so the downside is understated.

assumption_challenges.assumption: Discount rate of 10% and terminal growth of 3% in the base case. Bear terminal growth is 2% and bull is 3.5%.
assumption_challenges.why_questionable: A share-losing, cyclical, controlled company with a dual-class structure and a CFO change is given a 10% rate. A 3% perpetual growth rate implies it will outgrow inflation forever. Terminal value is about 73% of base value. On the scaled base each 1% change in the rate moves value a lot, so the point estimate is not robust.

assumption_challenges.assumption: The 'net cash' and strong-balance-sheet claim (moat and management sections).
assumption_challenges.why_questionable: Cash is $8.37B and total debt including leases is $11.1B, so net debt is about $2.8B. Excluding leases, debt of $7.9B is roughly equal to cash. The valuation correctly subtracts net debt, so the qualitative text contradicts the model. The same section cites leverage of about 2x. $2.0B of debt is current. There are also $15.5B of endorsement obligations, $4.9B of product purchase obligations and $2.4B of other purchase obligations, which are fixed commitments on a falling revenue base.

assumption_challenges.assumption: Management rated 'average' and the moat 'narrow', with Performance growth and Pace as catalysts.
assumption_challenges.why_questionable: The record is below average on capital allocation. Buybacks were done at about 3x the current price, the dividend is uncovered, and capex rose 59% to $684M while FCF fell. Restructuring is recurring and the CFO changed right after the 10-K. Performance growth of high single digits on about $16B (roughly $1.2B a year) is small next to declines of 10–28% in other segments. Pace savings are about $0.5B a year, pre-reinvestment.

assumption_challenges.assumption: Trailing P/E of 16.4 and forward P/E of 20.0 show a reasonable or cheap valuation.
assumption_challenges.why_questionable: Trailing EPS of about $2.08 will not repeat. FY27 guidance of $1.15–1.35 implies about 25–30x. The forward P/E of 20 implies forward EPS of about $1.70, which is above the guided range. The filings analysis also says the source of the forward P/E is not provided, so it looks stale or inconsistent with guidance. Trailing earnings also include the $986M tariff credit.

assumption_challenges.assumption: Returns on capital are high (ROE 21.6%, company ROIC 18.7%).
assumption_challenges.why_questionable: ROE is inflated by about $12B of buybacks that shrank equity, and ROE is about 20% on my own figures ($3.1B / $15.2B). The company's ROIC definition nets out all cash and includes leases. Through the cycle, EBIT margin fell from 12.7% to 8.3% and FCF margin from about 12.9% to 4.7%. P/B of 3.4 on a shrinking-margin business is not cheap.

inconsistencies_found: The valuation's base FCF of $4.023B is not any reported figure. It equals the FY24–FY26 average. The text elsewhere uses FY26 FCF of $2,184M for the 4.2% yield, dividend coverage and the margin analysis. The model and the narrative use different FCFs, and the model's is 84% higher.

The filings summary cites price of $34.61 and market cap of about $51.4B. The market data shows $34.045 and $50.57B. P/B is 3.45 in one place and 3.40 in the other, and forward P/E is 20.3 versus 20.01. The inputs come from different dates or sources, and the valuation's upside is computed on $34.045.
The forward P/E of 20.0 implies forward EPS of about $1.70. FY27 adjusted EPS guidance is $1.15–1.35, which implies about 25–30x. The two cannot both be right.

The 6% growth path is not consistent with guided FY27 revenue down high single digits, with Q1 at -4% and EPS about 40% lower. The base case also lies above the growth rationale's own 'low confidence' caveat and its list of arguments against.
'Net cash' (moat and management text) conflicts with the model, which subtracts $11.1B of debt and leases against $8.4B of cash, a net debt of about $2.8B. The same text cites leverage of about 2x.

Gross margin is described as up 0.2 points in FY26 and up 60 bps in Q1. FY26 includes the $986M one-time credit, which is about 210 bps of gross margin. Ex-credit, FY26 margin is down about 190 bps. In Q1, 40 of the 60 bps is attributed to FX. 'Margin recovery' is listed as a catalyst, but the underlying evidence is weaker than presented.

The filings analysis flags receivables growing 25.7% and sales reserves falling 13% with higher returns and discounts. It still treats FY26 OCF weakness as mostly timing (the IEEPA receivable). Excluding that item, receivables were still up about 11% against wholesale growth of 6% and revenue growth of 0.2%, and the Q1 filing shows other offsets. Yet the base case assumes FCF recovers.

Capital allocation is called 'mixed' with 'net cash a plus', but the same text says buybacks were done at about 3x today's price, the dividend exceeds FCF and capex rose 59%. A better label is 'poor' rather than 'average'.

Market Data total debt is $11,125M and the balance sheet total including leases is $11,072M, a small mismatch. Also, FY23 cannot be reconciled to the provided filings. Four years of FCF history are used, but only three years are verified, and the base FCF covers FY24–FY26.

The industry growth figure (7.2% in 2025) is from a low-quality source, and the competitor growth rates (On 30%, New Balance 20% and others) are also low-quality. The moat conclusion leans on third-party sites such as koalagains and founderpin, while the quantitative thesis uses none of the industry data. Industry growth is listed as 'unknown' elsewhere.
skeptic.severity_reason: The bullish +27% base-case upside depends on a $4.0B starting FCF that is 84% above reported FY26 FCF of $2.18B. Rebased to FY26 FCF, the model gives about $23 for base and about $13 for bear, and even the bull case roughly equals the current $34 price. On top of that, FY27 guidance implies about a 40% EPS decline and the dividend of about $2.4B is uncovered by FCF and by guided earnings. FY26 profit is flattered by a one-time $986M tariff credit. Share loss, an unproven turnaround, a CFO exit and weak governance give public holders little protection. This is mostly a valuation-base error, so 'major' is a judgment call, but the thesis as built should not be relied on.
